newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed despite index bounce.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed despite index bounce.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index gained, but the broader market ended mixed in moderate dealings on Tuesday as weaker commodity prices dragged many issues down.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index climbed 53.25 points to close at 6490.96. Trading totaled 92.8 million shares, worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).

Toronto rose amid New York's 153-point rebound to 7758 points after Monday's 192-point sell-off. "We weren't down as much as they were yesterday, so we aren't up as much," said Yorkton Securities trader Pier Donnini.
Declining issues edged out advancers 498 to 481, while 312 ended even.
Weak commodity prices such as gold bullion pressured many stocks, analysts said. "Golds are a persistent problem," Donnini said.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes added points, led by banks, transportation and media. Slipping sectors included conglomerates and golds.

Financial issues and other takeover targets grabbed investor attention on Tuesday. "If you look at the rest of the companies, nothing much happened," said Maison Placements Canada trader Rolie Bradley.

Bank of Nova Scotia, the nation's fourth largest, rose 2.25 to a 52-week high of 60.05 after news that it offered to acquire National Trustco Inc., the last large family-owned trust, in a deal valued at C$1.25 billion ($899 million).
In another move by a Canadian bank, takeover target London Insurance Group said it was in merger talks with the country's largest bank, Royal Bank of Canada.
London Insurance added 2.80 to 26.30, while Royal Bank rose 1.15 to a 52-week high of 63.15.
Analysts saw the moves as bids by the banks to expand beyond the traditional banking and brokerage businesses that Canada's major banks dominate.

Shares in newspaper chain Southam Inc. closed 1.25 higher at 23.50. Publisher Hollinger Inc.'s C$23.50 ($16.92) a share bid failed to spark a fire under Southam's minority shareholders, who rejected it late on Monday.
